newsitem.title: UK: Alliance Trust sees wider investor interest.
newsitem.headline: Alliance Trust sees wider investor interest.

text.p: The Alliance Trust Plc said on Monday there were signs that equity market interest was broadening outside of the leading shares and that value in some smaller stocks will be recognised.
"The expansion of world money and the pervasive influence of index funds has particularly inflated the valuation of the leading stocks," it said in its interim results.
Alliance raised net assets by 9.2 percent to a record 1.48 billion stg over the six months to end-July. The FTSE all-share index rose 9.9 percent in the same period.
It raised it interim dividend 8.8 percent to 18.5 pence and said it expected an increase in the final dividend.
It said the world economy and financial markets continue to be driven by the U.S., where the news had been encouraging, with economic growth cooling to what seems a sustainable level.

"Euphoric equity markets have, however, already priced in much of this relatively benign background. That leaves little room for disappointment in a world where there are many local problems and competition makes underlying profits growth increasingly difficult."

Alliance said its caution about valuation levels was evident in a lack of gearing and holding three percent in cash, which should enable it to take opportunities in "what will remain generally volatile markets."
The trust was 51 percent weighted in the UK, 25 percent in the North America, 11 percent in continental Europe and 10 percent in the Far East at end-July.
